neighbours.label: the word that closes an 'overdue / deserved' idiom: 'about time', 'high time', 'teach someone a lesson'
fire: The council finally repaired the bridge, and residents said it was about time.
My brother cleaned his room without being asked. About time, if you ask me.
Many voters feel it is high time the government listened to farmers.
After ten years of delays, it's high time the stadium was finished.
That bully keeps pushing kids around; somebody needs to teach him a lesson.
The coach benched the star player to teach the whole team a lesson.
When the train arrived on schedule for once, a passenger muttered, "About time."
She told her landlord it was high time he fixed the broken heater.
quiet: The council finally repaired the bridge, and residents gathered to watch the opening.
My brother cleaned his room in about an hour on Sunday afternoon.
Many voters spent a long time waiting in line outside the polling station.
After ten years of delays, the stadium opened on time for the first match.
That teacher keeps the kids busy; the history lesson runs until noon.
The coach prepared a video lesson on defence for the whole team.
When the train arrived, a passenger checked the time on his watch.
She told her landlord the heater broke last time it snowed.

notes: Card top: 'high time', 'about time', 'teach that guy a lesson', 'a good cry'. Probe: idiomatic 'about time'/'high time'/'teach a lesson' fire, literal 'time'/'lesson' do not.
